title: Coherent temporal filtering of multimode parametric down-conversion using a quantum pulse gate
authors: Abhinandan Bhattacharjee, Patrick Folge, Laura Serino, Sebastian Lengeling, Benjamin Brecht, Christine Silberhorn
abstract: Spectrally pure and indistinguishable single photons are essential for quantum network platforms, where high-visibility interference underpins many quantum information protocols. However, most practical single-photon sources emit spectrally multimode states with reduced purity. Conventional spectral intensity filtering can partially improve purity but cannot select a well-defined temporal mode (TM). Here, we demonstrate coherent temporal filtering of a multimode parametric down-conversion (PDC) source using a quantum pulse gate (QPG) and benchmark its performance against conventional intensity filtering. The generated PDC photons exhibit strong spectral correlations, rendering extraction of pure heralded photons from the pair a challenge. We demonstrate that QPG filtering consistently generates heralded photons with purities above 0.90 regardless of the filter shape. Contrariwise, using spectral intensity filters yields mixed photons. Photon purities are probed with chronocyclic Q-function tomography. Furthermore, we demonstrate the versatility of QPG filtering by extracting structured TMs, including superposition of picosecond time bins. These results establish the QPG as a practical coherent filtering tool for quantum network applications.
summary: The paper introduces and validates the use of a Quantum Pulse Gate (QPG) for coherently filtering multimode parametric down-conversion sources. This technique successfully projects heralded signal photons into spectrally pure, well-defined temporal modes with high fidelity. The results conclusively show that this coherent method vastly outperforms conventional intensity filtering, which degrades photon purity by introducing mixed states.
main_problem: The challenge is generating spectrally pure and indistinguishable single photons from multimode sources, which is crucial for quantum network applications.
main_result: Coherent temporal filtering using a Quantum Pulse Gate (QPG) successfully generates heralded photons with high purity (>0.90), whereas conventional intensity filtering results in mixed states.
method: The authors compare QPG-based coherent filtering against standard spectral intensity filtering by analyzing the resulting photon state's spectral density matrix and chronocyclic Q-function.
model_or_system: The system utilizes a time-frequency entangled pair source via parametric down-conversion (PDC). The core comparison is between projecting the idler photon onto a specific temporal mode using a QPG versus simple spectral amplitude filtering.
key_observables: Photon purity ($\mathcal{F}$), Spectral Density Matrix ($\Gamma$), and Chronocyclic $Q$-function ($\mathcal{F}(\Omega, 	au)$).
important_parameters: Filter bandwidth, coherence properties (single TM vs. multimode mixture), and the resulting spectral purity.
main_assumptions: Conventional intensity filtering cannot control relative phase or select a well-defined temporal mode; minor deviations in QPG performance are attributed to finite measurement resolution or pump shaping limitations.
figures_summary: Figures conceptually distinguish coherent (single TM transmission) vs. incoherent (spectral intensity transmission, phase erasure) filtering setups and show reconstructed spectral purity ($\mathcal{F}$) versus filter bandwidth for both methods.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for pure single photons; it then details the theoretical comparison between QPG-mediated coherent projection and conventional incoherent filtering using mathematical formalisms (JSA, $\Gamma$ matrix); finally, it presents experimental results demonstrating superior purity and programmability with the QPG.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses a key hardware bottleneck in quantum networking—the preparation of high-quality single photons—by providing a robust, coherent filtering mechanism applicable to existing PDC sources.

A Ti:Sapphire oscillator with a repetition rate of 76 MHz, a central wavelength of 771.9 nm, and a spectral bandwidth of 0.1 nm pumps a waveguide-integrated type-0 PDC source, which generates TF entangled photon pairs. The PDC source is a 1 cm long periodically poled titanium-in-diﬀused LiNbO3 waveguide operated at a temperature of 433 K.
